column1: # What the Guest Agent's glob matches: globset 0.4.21 with a literal separator. Each line is
# name, pattern, the paths that must match and the paths that must not, tab-separated, the paths of
# a column separated by "|". A line whose paths columns are "!" is a pattern that must be refused.
# The paths are relative to the directory searched. The Guest Agent's tests and the in-memory
# Guest's tests read one copy each, and `make test` fails unless the two are the same file.
a literal is the whole path, not a substring
star stays within a segment
star matches nothing at all
question mark is one character of a segment
question mark is one byte, so not a two-byte character
two question marks match a two-byte character
star matches a multi-byte character
double star at the start crosses segments
double star at the start matches a whole segment name
double star in the middle crosses zero or more segments
double star at the end matches what is below
double star alone matches every path
double star and a separator alone match every path
double star that ends a name is two stars
double star inside a name is two stars
double star that starts a name is two stars
double star after a separator and before a name is two stars
alternates choose between literals
alternates nest
an alternate may hold a separator
an alternate may hold a star, which stays within a segment
an alternate may start with a double star
an alternate may end with a double star
a double star after an alternate opens crosses segments
an empty alternate at the end is dropped
an empty alternate at the start is dropped
a nested empty alternate is dropped
a group of no alternate is no pattern at all
an escaped comma is a literal in an alternate
a comma outside alternates is a literal
a closing brace in a class is a literal
a class matches one of its characters
a class holds a range
a class negates with an exclamation mark
a class negates with a caret
a negated class matches a separator
a negated class is one byte, so not a two-byte character
a class may hold a separator
a first closing bracket is a literal
a first closing bracket after a negation is a literal
a trailing dash is a literal
a leading dash is a literal
a dash after a range extends the range
a class holds a two-byte character as bytes
a closing bracket outside a class is a literal
a backslash makes a star a literal
a backslash makes a question mark a literal
a backslash makes a bracket a literal
a backslash before an ordinary character is that character
a double backslash is one backslash
an escaped separator is a separator
an unclosed alternate group
an unopened alternate group
a dangling backslash
an unclosed class
an invalid range
